| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites. |

- KServe
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- FIPS posture for workbenches, pipelines, and training (separate strategies)
- Common Criteria certification

None on scope — but note that lab scheduling and review-board cadence are

# Onboard Platform Operator midstream repository

## Description

Create the midstream repository for the Platform Operator component under the
opendatahub-io organization so that its FIPS-related changes can be developed,
built, and released through the standard midstream workflow. The Platform
Operator has no architecture context file in the platform inventory, so this
decomposition treats it as a component not yet onboarded; provisioning the
repository is the first step of its onboarding chain.

## Scope

- Create the Platform Operator midstream repository under opendatahub-io,
  importing the upstream sources needed to build the operator images.
- Apply the repository conventions used by the other midstream serving
  components (branch layout, ownership files, CI triggers).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Platform Operator midstream repository exists under the opendatahub-io
  GitHub organization with the standard branch and convention setup matching
  the other midstream serving components.
- The operator container image builds reproducibly from source in the new
  repository.

## HLR Traceability

Enables HLR-1 (FIPS-correct serving-stack images): the Platform Operator
FIPS implementation needs this repository. Inherits P0 from the HLR-1 work it
enables.

# License validation for Platform Operator dependencies

## Description

Run license scanning over the upstream Platform Operator source tree and its
full transitive dependency set so the component is cleared for midstream
distribution and any license constraints are known before the FIPS
implementation locks in dependency choices. The scan deliberately runs against
the upstream sources and is not ordered against the midstream repository
provisioning — the two proceed in parallel.

## Scope

- Configure and run license scanning over the upstream Platform Operator
  source tree and the transitive dependencies of its image builds.
- Resolve, remediate, or document-with-exception every license finding.
- Record the scanning configuration so it can be reused in the build
  pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The license scan covers the complete transitive dependency tree pulled in
  by the operator image builds.
- Every flagged license is resolved, remediated, or covered by a documented
  and approved exception.
- The scanning configuration is committed so subsequent builds can re-run it.

## HLR Traceability

Enables HLR-1 (FIPS-correct serving-stack images): the Platform Operator
FIPS implementation is gated on dependency choices being license-cleared.
Inherits P0 from the HLR-1 work it enables.

# FIPS 140-3 compliance for Platform Operator images

## Description

Implement the Platform Operator changes required for the model serving stack
to run on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic
modules: the operator's own images must carry no non-validated crypto in the
request path, and the operator must deploy and manage the serving stack
correctly under FIPS cluster policy.

## Scope

- Audit the Platform Operator images for non-validated cryptographic library
  usage and replace it with validated crypto modules.
- Verify the operator deploys and manages the serving stack correctly on
  FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters (scheduling, rollouts, upgrades).
- Ship the changes through the operator's midstream repository and Konflux
  build pipeline provisioned for this component.

This epic runs in parallel with the Konflux pipeline onboarding for the
operator repository — there is deliberately no ordering between them. The
coupling is enforced by the build-pipeline-green acceptance criterion below:
the epic is not done until the operator image builds green through that
pipeline. The midstream repository itself is a prerequisite: development of
these changes begins once the operator's midstream repository exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Platform Operator images contain no non-validated cryptographic libraries
  in the request path (validated modules only).
- The operator deploys, upgrades, and manages the serving stack correctly on
  a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster (end-to-end functional verification).
- Build pipeline green: the operator image builds successfully through its
  Konflux pipeline.
- License-cleared dependency tree is respected (no new unscanned
  dependencies introduced by the crypto changes).

## HLR Traceability

HLR-1 — all serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using
validated crypto modules (Platform Operator portion).

# FIPS 140-3 remediation of KServe and serving data plane images

## Description

Replace non-validated cryptographic library usage in the KServe component
images and the serving data plane images with validated crypto modules, so
that all serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift
clusters with no non-validated crypto in the request path.

## Scope

- Audit the KServe component images and the serving data plane images to
  produce a module inventory of the cryptographic libraries each image links
  (this inventory is also an input to the compliance evidence package).
- Replace non-validated crypto library usage with validated modules across
  the in-scope images, carrying changes midstream as needed.
- Verify request-path functionality on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters
  (inference requests succeed end-to-end in both serverless and raw
  deployment modes).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A module inventory exists listing the cryptographic libraries linked into
  every in-scope serving-stack image (KServe components and serving data
  plane).
- No in-scope image links a non-validated cryptographic library in the
  request path.
- The serving stack serves inference requests correctly on a FIPS-enabled
  OpenShift cluster (end-to-end verification).
- All remediated images build green through their existing Konflux
  pipelines.

## HLR Traceability

HLR-1 — all serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using
validated crypto modules (KServe and serving data plane portion). The module
inventory produced here feeds HLR-2's evidence package.

# CI gating check for FIPS crypto regressions in serving-stack builds

## Description

A gating CI check that fails any serving-stack build which reintroduces
non-validated cryptographic library usage, protecting the remediated FIPS
baseline of the serving stack against regressions.

## Scope

- Implement a build-time check (image/dependency scan) that detects
  non-validated crypto usage in serving-stack image builds.
- Wire the check as a gating (build-failing, not advisory) step into the
  serving-stack build pipelines, covering the KServe and Platform Operator
  build pipelines.
- Provide a test fixture that demonstrably fails the check (a deliberately
  non-compliant image).

This epic is developed in parallel with the serving-stack FIPS remediation —
there is deliberately no ordering edge between them. The operational coupling
is an acceptance criterion below: the check must pass against the remediated
images, i.e. the gate is enabled on the remediated baseline rather than
before it exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The check detects non-validated crypto usage in a serving-stack image
  build and fails that build (verified against a deliberately non-compliant
  test image).
- The check passes on serving-stack builds whose images use only validated
  crypto modules (the remediated baseline).
- The check is gating in every serving-stack build pipeline it covers — a
  build with non-validated crypto cannot merge or release.

## HLR Traceability

HLR-3 — CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any serving-stack
build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage.

# FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package and certification submission

## Description

Assemble the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package for the model serving
stack — module inventory, build attestations, and test results — and carry it
through the mandatory security review board sign-off and submission to the
external accredited certification lab.

## Scope

- Assemble the module inventory from the remediated serving-stack images
  (KServe components, serving data plane, and Platform Operator images).
- Collect signed build attestations from the serving-stack build pipelines,
  including the operator's Konflux pipeline.
- Compile the FIPS-mode test results produced by the remediation work.
- Package the evidence per the certification lab's requirements.
- Submit the package through the security review board to the external
  certification lab and address triage feedback.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The evidence package contains the module inventory, build attestations,
  and FIPS-mode test results, covering every serving-stack image in scope.
- The evidence package has been submitted to the security review board;
  review feedback is addressed and sign-off is recorded.
- The evidence package has been submitted to the external certification lab
  and accepted for review (triaged).

## Risks / Notes

- The accredited lab's historical turnaround is six to nine months, and both
  lab scheduling and review-board cadence are externally controlled — they
  cannot be compressed by engineering effort. This is schedule risk on the
  certification outcome, not a deliverable of this epic: the acceptance
  criteria above are written at the engineering completion point (package
  assembled, sign-off recorded, submitted and triaged).

## HLR Traceability

HLR-2 — a compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations,
test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to
the external certification lab.

# Document FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites

## Description

Author user-facing documentation stating the FIPS support posture of the
model serving stack and the cluster prerequisites for running it on
FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters, reflecting the implemented and submitted
compliance work.

## Scope

Content outline (authored inside the documentation set for the serving
stack):

- FIPS support posture of the model serving stack: what runs on validated
  cryptographic modules, what has been submitted for certification, and the
  explicit boundaries (workbenches, pipelines, and training FIPS posture and
  Common Criteria are out of scope per the strategy).
- Cluster prerequisites: FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters and any operator or
  serving-stack configuration required for FIPS operation.
- Support limitations and guidance for public-sector FIPS deployments.
